metadata.title: SDS-PAGE (Laemmli Discontinuous Denaturing Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis)
metadata.purpose: Separate proteins by molecular weight under denaturing conditions on a discontinuous (Laemmli) polyacrylamide gel: proteins are coated with SDS, stacked in a 5% stacking gel, then resolved in a 10% resolving gel and visualized by Coomassie staining.
metadata.scope: Standard reducing Laemmli SDS-PAGE on a Bio-Rad mini gel system for proteins >~10 kDa. Very small proteins (<10 kDa) need gradient or Tricine-SDS gels and are out of scope. Gel casting recipes given for 10% resolving / 5% stacking; the acrylamide percentage is adjusted for other size ranges.
metadata.estimatedTime: ~2.5-3 h (gel casting + polymerization ~1 h, sample prep ~20 min, run + stain)
beforeYouBegin: Quantify protein (e.g. BCA assay) so equal amounts are loaded per lane.
Prepare 10x running buffer and 2x SDS sample buffer in advance (see materials).
Make 10% ammonium persulfate fresh (store at 4 C up to a month); add APS and TEMED only immediately before pouring each gel.
Change the ddH2O:acrylamide ratio to cast a different resolving-gel percentage.

materials.name: 30% acrylamide/bis (37.5:1)
materials.hazard: Unpolymerized acrylamide is a potent neurotoxin

materials.name: 20% (w/v) SDS
materials.specification: Detergent stock for gels and buffers

materials.name: 10% ammonium persulfate (APS)
materials.rawText: 10% ammonium persulfate (make it fresh and store at 4 C up to a month)

materials.name: TEMED
materials.specification: Polymerization catalyst; add immediately before pouring
materials.rawText: TEMED (add it right before pour the gel)

materials.name: Isopropanol
materials.specification: Overlay to flatten the resolving gel surface during polymerization
materials.rawText: Add a small layer of isopropanol to the top of the gel prior to polymerization

materials.name: 2x SDS protein sample buffer
materials.specification: Per 10 mL: 1.25 mL 1 M Tris-HCl pH 6.8, 4.0 mL 10% SDS, 2.0 mL glycerol, 0.5 mL 0.5 M EDTA, 4 mg bromophenol blue, 0.2 mL beta-mercaptoethanol; ddH2O to 10 mL
materials.hazard: Contains beta-mercaptoethanol (toxic, foul-smelling) - use a fume hood
materials.rawText: 2x SDS protein sample buffer: 1.25 ml 1 M Tris-HCl (pH 6.8), 4.0 ml 10% (w/v) SDS, 2.0 ml glycerol, 0.5 ml 0.5 M EDTA, 4 mg bromophenol blue, 0.2 ml b-mercaptoethanol (14.3 M); bring to 10 ml with ddH2O

materials.name: 10x Tris-glycine-SDS running buffer
materials.specification: Per liter (10x): 30.3 g Tris base, 144.0 g glycine, 10.0 g SDS; = 25 mM Tris, 192 mM glycine, 0.1% SDS at 1x
materials.rawText: 10x running buffer: 30.3 g Tris-base, 144.0 g glycine, 10.0 g SDS; ddH2O up to 1 liter

materials.name: Coomassie Brilliant Blue stain
materials.specification: For visualizing >=0.2 ug protein/band; use silver stain for lower amounts
materials.rawText: typically use Coomassie blue staining ... Otherwise, use silver staining

equipment.name: Vertical mini gel electrophoresis cell + power supply
equipment.settings: 200 V constant until the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel

equipment.name: Gel casting stand + mini gel cassette (glass plates, spacers, comb)

samples.name: Protein sample (quantified lysate/extract)
samples.description: Equalized protein amounts per lane based on BCA result

samples.name: Denatured, reduced protein sample
samples.description: Sample mixed 1:1 with 2x SDS sample buffer and boiled at 95 C

samples.name: Resolved protein band pattern in gel
samples.description: Size-separated proteins after electrophoresis and staining

tables.title: Gel casting recipes (per gel)
tables.note: Change the ddH2O:acrylamide ratio to cast other resolving-gel percentages. Add APS then TEMED last and pour immediately.

steps.action: Assemble a clean, dry gel cassette on the casting stand per manufacturer instructions.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Clean and completely dry glass plates, combs, and spacers are required. Assemble gel cassette.

steps.action: Mix the 10% resolving gel (5 mL total), adding APS then TEMED last; pour between the plates to ~0.7 cm below the comb.
steps.criticalNotes: Add TEMED right before pouring; mix and transfer quickly before polymerization.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Prepare 10% lower gel: 2 ml ddH2O, 1.67 ml 30% acrylamide/Bis, 1.25 ml 1.5 M Tris (pH 8.8), 25 ul 20% SDS, 25 ul 10% APS, 2.5 ul TEMED.

steps.action: Overlay the resolving gel with a small layer of isopropanol and allow it to polymerize.
steps.expectedResult: Flat, level resolving-gel surface after polymerization.

steps.action: Remove isopropanol and rinse with ddH2O; mix the 5% stacking gel (3 mL total), pour to fill, and insert the comb.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Prepare stacking gel (5%): 2.088 ml dH2O, 0.506 ml 30% acrylamide/Bis, 0.375 ml 1 M Tris (pH 6.8), 15 ul 20% SDS, 15 ul 10% APS, 1.5 ul TEMED.

steps.action: Allow the stacking gel to solidify, then carefully remove the comb.
steps.criticalNotes: Cast gels can be stored with combs in place, wrapped in plastic with wet tissue, at 4 C for 1-2 weeks.

steps.action: Normalize protein amounts across samples based on the BCA assay result.
Add an equal volume of 2x SDS sample buffer to each sample, mix, and boil at 95 C.

parameters.rawText: Add the same volume of 2x protein sample buffer

steps.criticalNotes: Stored samples in buffer can be reheated at 95 C for 5 min before reuse.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Add the same volume of 2x protein sample buffer ... boil the samples at 95 C heating block module for 10 min.

steps.action: Spin samples at maximum speed and hold at room temperature until loading.

parameters.rawText: Spin the samples at the maximal speed for 1 min

steps.action: Mount the cassette in the electrode assembly and tank; fill wells and the inner/outer chambers with 1x running buffer.

sourceReferences.excerpt: Pour some 1x electrophoresis running buffer ... Add enough buffer to fill the wells of the gel.

steps.action: Load equal amounts of each denatured sample and 10 uL of protein MW marker into the wells.

parameters.rawText: load 10 ul of protein MW marker

sourceReferences.excerpt: Slowly load the same amount of protein samples into each well as well as load 10 ul of protein MW marker.

steps.action: Connect to the power supply and run at 200 V until the bromophenol blue dye front reaches the bottom of the gel.

parameters.rawText: until the dye front reaches the bottom of the gel (~30-45 min on a mini gel)

steps.expectedResult: Proteins stacked then resolved; dye front at the gel bottom.
steps.criticalNotes: The Bio-protocol source states 'connect to the power supply' but does not give voltage/time; 200 V constant is the Bio-Rad Mini-PROTEAN standard.

steps.action: Stain to visualize protein bands: use Coomassie blue for >=0.2 ug protein/band, otherwise silver stain (down to ~5 ng).

sourceReferences.excerpt: If protein of interest is about 0.2 ug or more, typically use Coomassie blue staining. Otherwise, use silver staining ... as little as 5 ng.

branches.condition: If protein of interest is >=0.2 ug use Coomassie blue; if lower, use silver staining.

controls.name: Molecular-weight marker
controls.description: Prestained ladder in one lane to assign apparent molecular weights.

controls.name: Equal-loading normalization
controls.description: Load identical protein amounts (per BCA) in every lane so band intensities are comparable.

expectedOutputs: A gel with proteins resolved into discrete bands, sized against the MW marker.
A stained, imageable record of the band pattern for each sample.

troubleshooting.solution: Make 10% APS fresh; add both APS and TEMED and pour immediately

troubleshooting.cause: Overloaded protein; incomplete denaturation; run too fast/hot
troubleshooting.solution: Reduce load; ensure full boil in sample buffer; keep voltage/temperature moderate

troubleshooting.cause: Stacking gel too short or wrong pH buffers
troubleshooting.solution: Confirm 1.0 M Tris pH 6.8 (stacking) and 1.5 M Tris pH 8.8 (resolving); pour adequate stacking gel

safety: Unpolymerized acrylamide/bis is a potent neurotoxin - wear gloves and handle stocks and liquid gel with care.
beta-mercaptoethanol and TEMED give off harmful vapors - work in a fume hood.
Ammonium persulfate is an irritant; the running buffer contains SDS (irritant).
limitations: Denaturing, non-quantitative separation for proteins >~10 kDa; resolution of small proteins requires Tricine or gradient gels. Run voltage/time is taken from the Bio-Rad mini-gel standard, not the Bio-protocol source, which omits it.
